provenance.warning: Every row here is agent-collected. The per-row `verified` field is the collecting agent's own claim and is NOT equivalent to this repository's `read` grade. domains.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety (AF + CHA2DS2-VASc/VA anticoagulation; renal-conditioned DOAC dosing)

verdict.reasoning:
CLAIM 1 (asymmetry) is contradicted in this domain, and partly ill-posed here. Stroke prevention in AF barely has a drug-only axis - the clinical content is almost entirely of the form 'drug X in patients WITH condition Y'. Where I could compare, the condition-dependent axis survived operationalization repeatedly and at high fidelity: QOF AF007 (NI, primary document, executable Read/CTV3 rules), MIPS #326 (US, primary document, ICD-10-CM list), HIRA STR0020 (Korea, primary document, chart-abstraction definition), Scotland STU case finding (primary document, Read/SNOMED/DM&D). Four of five instruments I could read retained axis B. That is the opposite of the PIM-domain pattern.

CLAIM 2 (binding mechanism) is supported, and is the only claim that survives intact. Every retention I verified co-occurs with a binding the operating body authored AND applied in the executable definition: DoH NI authored AFIB_COD (G573.% excl. G5731/G5736), CHADVASC_COD (38DE0/XaY6i) with a value slot, and XORANTICOAG_COD, then applied them in numbered denominator rules; CMS/ACC-AHA authored the ICD-10-CM I48 list and G0043/G0044/G9929/G9931; Scotland's pharmacist/technician team 'maps each element of the criteria within the indicator to clinical codes ... read codes (which in turn map to SNOMED-CT codes) and the Dictionary of Medicines and Devices (DM&D)' and stores them in EScro; HIRA bound I63 and bought chart abstraction (조사표) for AF. Conversely the single clear loss - Scotland's National Therapeutic Indicators, which contain no AF-without-anticoagulant indicator - sits in the one appendix that supplies no technical specification at all. Claim 2 also gains a refinement: binding need not be a diagnosis-code value set. Korea's binding is an abstraction instrument; CMS's binding for the risk score is a single attestation HCPCS code. Both are 'authored operational definitions' and both worked.

CLAIM 3 (gradient toward payment) is contradicted. The two instruments closest to money are precisely the two with the most explicit, most machine-executable condition bindings in the whole domain: UK QOF (direct GP contract payment; AF007/AF008 pay on a denominator defined by AF diagnosis codes AND a coded CHA2DS2-VASc value) and US MIPS #326 (Medicare payment adjustment; denominator defined by nine ICD-10-CM codes with four coded condition-dependent exclusions). The predicted gradient appears only inside Scotland, where the AF-conditioned rule lives in decision support and is absent from the national comparative indicator set - and Scotland has no payment layer at all, having abolished QOF in 2016, so that observation cannot be read as loss-toward-payment.

One partial-loss finding does fit the spirit of Claims 1 and 3, at a finer grain: MIPS #326 binds AF (ICD-10-CM) and binds the risk-score RESULT (G9931) but never binds the five comorbidities that generate the score. The comorbidity conditions are printed as a clinician-facing table and then delegated to attestation. So within one payment measure, the codable single diagnosis was bound and the diffuse multi-condition construct was offloaded.

domains.contradictions:
Cases found that argue AGAINST the hypothesis, all from primary documents:

1. UK QOF AF007 (payment layer) retains the condition axis in full and codes it. VERBATIM: "Indicator AF007: In those patients with atrial fibrillation with a record of a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 2 or more, the percentage of patients who are currently treated with anticoagulation drug therapy" (DoH NI ruleset v34.0NI, health-ni.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/health/atrial-34.pdf). The denominator is executed as "Rule 1: If CHADVASC_VAL >= 2 OR [If CHADVASC_DAT = Null AND (If CHAD_DAT != Null AND If CHAD_VAL >= 2)]". Directly refutes Claim 3 and, for this domain, Claim 1.

2. CMS MIPS #326 (payment layer, 2026, Version 10.0) retains the condition axis and authored four separate condition-dependent exclusion codes. VERBATIM: "Diagnosis for atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter on date of encounter (ICD-10-CM): I48.0, I48.3, I48.4, I48.11, I48.19, I48.20, I48.21, I48.91, I48.92"; "Patients with moderate or severe mitral stenosis: G0044"; "Patients with mechanical prosthetic heart valve: G0043". Refutes Claim 3.

3. HIRA (Korea) retained the AF-conditioned rule where the PIM prior said Korea drops axis B. VERBATIM: "지표 명칭 심방세동이 있는 환자의 항응고제 퇴원처방률 ... 분모 입원 전 또는 입원 중 심방세동이 있는 급성기 허혈성 뇌졸중 환자의 입원 건수". Korea did not degrade this to a drug-only "antithrombotic prescribed" rule; it kept BOTH STR0020 (AF-conditioned) and STR0021 (all ischaemic stroke). Refutes the generalisation drawn from Korea's 2022 PIM criteria.

4. Korea's binding is not a diagnosis-code value set at all, which complicates Claim 2's stated mechanism ("drugs arrive pre-coded... conditions do not"). HIRA's data source is VERBATIM "평가 자료원 의무기록자료(조사표)" - chart abstraction by survey form. The condition axis survived by being paid for in abstraction labour, not by being coded. Claim 2 is right that an authored operational definition is necessary; it is wrong if it requires that definition to be a terminology binding.

5. A structural contradiction to Claim 1 as a general law: in this domain the drug-only axis is nearly empty. There is no meaningful "avoid anticoagulant X in older adults" criterion to compare survival against. Claim 1 was derived from a domain (PIM/Beers/Korean PIM list) whose criteria are drug-indexed by construction. Testing "does A survive more than B" requires both axes to be present; here only B is present, and B survived.

What I looked for and did NOT find (so cannot report as contradiction either way): a national AF-anticoagulation instrument in which the condition axis was authored in consensus and then deleted in operationalization. I searched for it in Scotland (found the near-case, see below), Korea, England/NI, and the US. The nearest true loss is Scotland's National Therapeutic Indicators (Appendix C, 21 indicators, no AF-without-anticoagulant item; the only anticoagulant NTI is drug-drug: "Number of people prescribed an antiplatelet also prescribed an oral anticoagulant but without gastroprotection as a percentage of all people prescribed an oral anticoagulant"), and the partial loss inside MIPS #326 where the CHA2DS2-VASc constituent comorbidities are never code-bound. Both of those support the hypothesis; I report them here rather than burying them.

5. JAPAN IS ENTIRELY UNASSESSED. I reached no Japanese national instrument. The JCS 2020 arrhythmia pharmacotherapy guideline (j-circ.or.jp) 403'd, and I had no search budget left to locate an MHLW indicator specification, a 診療報酬 provision, or the 全日本病院協会 / 日本病院会 QI project stroke measures. The PIM-domain prior reported a Japanese axis-B loss; I could neither replicate nor refute that here.

6. Australia unassessed. The ACSQHC Atrial Fibrillation Clinical Care Standard page timed out twice.

I also established only that the manual's indicators feed "전문병원지정･평가, 의료질평가지원금 산정을 위한 평가"; I did NOT establish that acute stroke sits in HIRA's 가감지급 (value incentive) programme, so I classified it public-rating rather than payment.

8. STOPP/START v3 (2023) primary text not retrieved. START criterion A1/A2 (anticoagulant in chronic AF) is the canonical undertreatment consensus item for this domain and would strengthen the consensus-criteria section; I did not read it and did not quote it.

9. ESC 2021 Quality Indicators for AF (Arbelo et al.) not retrieved - only its citation inside the ESC 2024 reference list. That paper is the intermediate consensus-to-measure artefact for Europe.

10. VSAC/eCQM value sets for AF anticoagulation (Joint Commission STK-03 and any eCQM equivalent) not retrieved; manual.jointcommission.org returned 404 on the URL I tried and I had no search budget to find the correct release path. So I could not test whether the US hospital-quality (public-rating) layer binds the condition axis the way the US payment layer does - a gap directly relevant to Claim 3.

No counts were estimated anywhere. conditionCount is null for both consensus criteria because neither source presents a countable condition table analogous to the Beers drug-disease table, and I would have had to construct the count myself.
domains.newHypotheses:
DENOMINATOR-NECESSITY HYPOTHESIS (I think this explains both domains better than the drug/condition axis distinction).

A condition survives operationalization when it sits in the DENOMINATOR - when the measure cannot be computed at all without it - and is dropped when it sits only in a refinement, exclusion, or numerator qualifier that can be deleted while the measure still produces a number.

- PIM/Beers-type criteria are STOPP-shaped: "avoid drug X in patients with condition Y." The natural denominator is the drug-exposed population. The condition is a refinement. Delete it and you still have a publishable rate ("% of older adults on drug X"). It gets deleted.
- AF anticoagulation is START-shaped: "patients with AF and elevated risk who are NOT on an anticoagulant." The condition IS the denominator. Delete it and there is no measure, because the numerator event is the ABSENCE of a drug and absence has no population. It cannot be deleted, so a body is forced to author a binding, whatever the layer and whatever the cost.

This reframes Claim 2's mechanism. It is not that drugs arrive pre-coded and conditions do not; it is that undertreatment measures make the condition load-bearing while overtreatment measures make it optional. Predictions that would test this cheaply: (a) any START-type national indicator, in any domain, should show axis-B retention at the payment layer (statin in diabetes / SUPD, ACEi-ARB in HF, antiplatelet after MI); (b) any STOPP-type drug-disease avoidance rule should show axis-B loss even in jurisdictions that demonstrably CAN author bindings - England authored AFIB_COD for QOF AF007 in the same contract in which it did not operationalize the Beers drug-disease table, which is a within-jurisdiction control against "Korea/England lack terminology capacity."

CODABILITY HYPOTHESIS (secondary, and visible inside a single document). Atrial fibrillation is the easiest condition in medicine to bind: one ICD-10 family (I48.x), one clean SNOMED/Read hierarchy (G573.%), and it was already a QOF disease register before AF007 existed. The conditions that get dropped in the PIM domain - falls, delirium, chronic constipation, "history of" states - have no discrete coded representation. MIPS #326 shows the split inside one payment measure: AF got nine ICD-10-CM codes, mitral stenosis and mechanical valve got dedicated G-codes, and the five diffuse CHA2DS2-VASc comorbidities got no codes at all, collapsed instead into the attestation code G9931. So "condition axis" is not one thing; codability of the specific condition may do most of the work the axis distinction was doing.

REGISTER-PRECEDENCE HYPOTHESIS (third). Every retention I verified attaches to a condition that already had an independently maintained register or population frame: the QOF AF register (AF001), HIRA's acute-stroke assessment cohort (I63), Medicare's claims diagnosis stream. Axis B may survive wherever the binding was already paid for by some other programme, and fail wherever the indicator would have to fund the binding itself.

domains.domain: Opioid prescribing safety (dose thresholds, opioid–benzodiazepine co-prescription, opioids in patients with respiratory disease / prior overdose / substance use disorder)

verdict.reasoning: CLAIM 1 — SUPPORTED, and in a sharper form than the PIM prior. Across every national instrument I read primarily (NCQA HEDIS, CMS506v7, CMS Part D POS edits, CMS Star Ratings, English prescribing comparators, Korean MFDS standard), what is operationalised is always a DOSE THRESHOLD on a drug or a DRUG-DRUG pair. Not one instrument operationalises a drug-DISEASE trigger, even though CDC Recommendation 8 names sleep-disordered breathing, history of overdose, substance use disorder, renal/hepatic insufficiency, pregnancy and mental health conditions as risk-elevating. The asymmetry is therefore near-total on the trigger side. But the correct axis boundary in this domain is not drug-only vs condition-dependent; it is COMPUTABLE-FROM-DISPENSING vs NOT. Opioid+benzodiazepine co-prescription is nominally 'condition-dependent' in the task framing, but both arms are drugs, both arrive pre-coded from the claim or the order, and it survives everywhere (CDC Rec 11 -> CMS506v7 numerator -> CMS Part D POS edit -> MFDS 병용투여 clause). Classifying it as axis B would falsely weaken Claim 1; classifying it as axis A strengthens Claim 1 and is what the mechanism actually predicts. SECOND AND MORE INTERESTING FINDING: where the condition axis DOES survive, it survives only in the EXCULPATORY direction. Cancer, sickle cell disease, palliative care, hospice and opioid use disorder appear as denominator EXCLUSIONS in HEDIS and CMS506v7 and as exemptions in the Part D edits; 'in Persons Without Cancer' is even in the official Star Ratings measure titles. In no instrument does a condition ADD a patient to the numerator. This is a directional asymmetry the Binding-Survival Hypothesis does not currently name. It has an obvious economic reading: a false positive on a cancer or hospice patient produces a visible access harm with an identifiable complainant and a coverage-appeal path, so the operating body pays to bind that condition; a missed sleep-apnoea patient produces a statistical harm with no complainant, so nobody pays to bind it. CLAIM 2 — MIXED. The OUTCOME half is well supported: every instrument where the condition axis genuinely survives is one where the operating body authored AND applied a binding and said so in the specification (NCQA's Malignant Neoplasms / Sickle Cell / Palliative Care value sets; CMS's VSAC OIDs in CMS506v7). The instrument where CMS named the same conditions but authored NO binding — the Part D point-of-sale edits — degraded exactly as predicted, into 'sponsors are expected to develop specifications' and 'pharmacists may have existing knowledge'. And the drug axis arrives pre-coded everywhere: WHO ATC in Korea, SNOMED CT ingredient codes and dm+d in England, the NDC Medication List Directory in HEDIS, RxNorm-backed value sets in the eCQM. But the stated MECHANISM half is wrong as a general claim. 'Drugs arrive pre-coded as a by-product of dispensing/claiming; conditions do not' is false in claims systems: ICD-10-CM is on every US medical claim and KCD is on every Korean HIRA claim. The binding work is not code CREATION but code SELECTION and VALIDATION, and NCQA's own words show this precisely — the palliative-care exclusion was refined by 'using codes that indicate receipt of palliative care, not referral for palliative care' and 'requiring at least two occurrences of a palliative care code on different dates of service'. Meanwhile in England the barrier is neither codes nor selection but SUBSTRATE: practice-level prescribing data has no patient-level diagnosis at all, so no amount of authoring would help. So there are at least three distinct mechanisms hiding inside Claim 2 — code selection/validation cost (US retrospective measures), diagnosis absent from the transaction (US Part D POS, Korean dispensing-history checks), and diagnosis absent from the dataset entirely (English aggregate prescribing data). CLAIM 3 — CONTRADICTED in this domain. The instrument with the RICHEST condition binding I found anywhere is CMS506v7, which carries four condition value sets with published OIDs and sits in payment-linked hospital reporting. HEDIS opioid measures carry three condition value sets and feed NCQA health plan ratings, i.e. the public-rating layer. Meanwhile the layer FARTHEST from money in this domain — the English prescribing comparators — has ZERO condition axis, and Korea's national guideline, the farthest-from-money layer of all, never had one. That is the reverse of the predicted gradient. The one datum that fits Claim 3 is the Part D point-of-sale edit, the single closest-to-money instrument and the one where CMS declined to author a binding. But the better explanation for that one datum is not money-proximity: it is that a POS edit fires inside the NCPDP pharmacy claim transaction, where a diagnosis is simply not present, whereas HEDIS and eCQMs run retrospectively over the full medical claim or EHR record. Money-proximity and real-time-transaction-proximity are confounded in the PIM prior; in opioid safety they come apart, and the substrate variable wins.

domains.contradictions:
FOUR CONCRETE CONTRADICTIONS FOUND, ranked by how much they should move the hypothesis.

1. CLAIM 3 IS DIRECTLY CONTRADICTED BY CMS506v7. The eCQM 'Safe Use of Opioids – Concurrent Prescribing' is a payment-linked hospital reporting measure and carries the richest condition binding in the whole domain: Cancer Related Pain (2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1111.180), Sickle Cell Disease with and without Crisis (2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1111.175), Opioid Use Disorder (2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1111.171), Medications for Opioid Use Disorder (2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1046.269), plus palliative/hospice logic. Simultaneously, the two layers farthest from money in this domain (English prescribing comparators; Korea's national MFDS guideline) have NO condition axis at all. The gradient runs backwards. I looked specifically for this and could not explain it away.

2. THE TASK'S PREMISE ABOUT ENGLAND PINCER IS FALSE. I was asked to check 'England PINCER indicator on high-dose opioids'. PINCER's own published codelist registry (opencodelists.org/codelist/pincer/) contains 24 codelists covering NSAIDs/GI bleed, asthma, heart failure, renal function, lithium, methotrexate, amiodarone and antiplatelets — and zero opioid, morphine or benzodiazepine codelists. There is no PINCER opioid indicator. This matters because it removes what would have been the strongest axis-B-retained case in England, and because it shows that an existing, funded, demonstrably condition-binding CDS capability was NOT extended to opioids. Binding capability is evidently not sufficient for axis B to appear.

3. NCQA DELIBERATELY WITHHELD AN AVAILABLE BINDING. In the HEDIS MY2020 cross-cutting palliative-care exclusion proposal, NCQA applied the Palliative Care value set to Risk of Continued Opioid Use and Use of Opioids at High Dosage but explicitly refused to apply it to Use of Opioids from Multiple Providers, verbatim: 'Opioids from Multiple Providers (UOP) was not selected for inclusion, because individuals receiving palliative care are at increased risk for opioid use disorder and other medication errors if they receive prescriptions from multiple providers, and should be provided appropriate care coordination to reduce this risk.' The binding existed, was already authored, and cost nothing extra to apply — and was withheld on clinical grounds. Axis-B survival is therefore not a purely mechanical function of binding availability; a clinical judgement gate sits on top of it.

4. THE CONDITION AXIS SURVIVES AT THE NAME LEVEL EVEN WHERE THE MEASURE DIES. The 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes still carry the titles 'Use of Opioids at High Dosage in Persons Without Cancer (OHD)', 'Use of Opioids from Multiple Providers in Persons Without Cancer (OMP)' and 'Use of Opioids at High Dosage and from Multiple Providers in Persons Without Cancer (OHDMP)'. These are display-measure-only (DMD-prefixed identifiers throughout, never a star D## identifier) and absent from the current active set — 'opioid' appears on only 2 of 211 pages. So what was lost at the payment layer was not the condition axis specifically but the ENTIRE opioid measure family, axis and all. I cannot establish that the condition axis was the cause of retirement, and I flag this as a confound rather than counting it as Claim 3 support.

ADDITIONALLY, A MECHANISM-LEVEL CONTRADICTION: Claim 2's rationale asserts 'conditions do not arrive pre-coded'. This is false in claims-based systems. ICD-10-CM rides on every US medical claim and KCD on every Korean HIRA claim, as a by-product of claiming, exactly as drug codes do. NCQA's own description of its work is code SELECTION and VALIDATION ('using codes that indicate receipt of palliative care, not referral'; 'requiring at least two occurrences ... on different dates of service'), not code creation. The mechanism should be restated in terms of whether the diagnosis is present in the specific data stream the instrument reads at the moment it fires.

NOT FOUND, despite looking: I searched specifically for any national instrument in any jurisdiction that operationalises a condition as a TRIGGER for an opioid rule — opioid prescribed to a patient with sleep-disordered breathing, COPD/respiratory disease, prior overdose, or substance use disorder. I found none in the primary documents I could read. If such an instrument exists (VA STORM and the VA Opioid Safety Initiative are the most likely candidates, and Canada's CIHI and Japan's MHLW are unchecked), it would be the strongest available refutation of Claim 1 in this domain and should be the first target of any follow-up.
domains.unassessable:
DOCUMENTS I COULD NOT OBTAIN, AND WHY:

1. PQA technical specifications for COB (Concurrent Use of Opioids and Benzodiazepines), OHD-AD and OMP. PQA's specification documents are member-restricted; p4qm.org/measures/3389 returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, pqaalliance.org redirects to pqa.org and the retirement summary PDF then 404s, and pqa.org/measures-overview carries no measure-level detail. I therefore did NOT verify PQA's own exclusion wording or whether PQA authored the code lists. Everything I report about the PQA-derived measures comes from NCQA's adaptation of them, which NCQA states verbatim: 'Adapted with financial support from CMS and with permission from the measure developer, Pharmacy Quality Alliance (PQA).' Treat PQA's authorship of the cancer/sickle-cell/hospice bindings as unverified. This is the single most important gap, because PQA is the original author of the US opioid measure family.

2. Australia — ACSQHC Opioid Analgesic Stewardship in Acute Pain Clinical Care Standard (2022) and its indicator specifications in AIHW METeOR (content/755544). The ACSQHC indicators page timed out twice at 60s, the standard PDF returned an empty body to curl, and METeOR is Cloudflare-gated. I have only a secondary search summary indicating an indicator on co-prescribed CNS depressant medicines. Not reported as a finding. This is a real loss: METeOR is a national indicator registry that publishes formal data-element definitions, so it is exactly the kind of body that would author a binding, and Australia would have been a clean independent test of Claim 2.

3. Korea — HIRA DUR 점검기준. I could not obtain the primary document listing the DUR check categories. The HIRA user guide I retrieved (BZ202405300045027.pdf) is an installation manual, and hira.or.kr/cms/guide_busi/03/03/index.html carries only a one-line description. One search summary asserted that 질병금기 (disease contraindication) is among the DUR categories; I regard that as unreliable and did NOT report it. Whether Korea's national real-time CDS has any diagnosis-based check, and whether it includes an opioid+benzodiazepine 병용금기 pair, is unresolved. Under hypothesis 1 above I would predict no disease axis, but that is a prediction, not a finding.

4. Korea — HIRA/MOHW 요양급여 적용기준 for opioid analgesics. Secondary sources indicate the coverage rules split explicitly on cancer versus non-cancer pain, with fentanyl capped at 25 mcg/h in non-cancer patients. If accurate, this is a PAYMENT-layer instrument that retains a condition axis and rides on KCD codes already present on the claim — a further direct contradiction of Claim 3 and a clean demonstration that diagnoses do arrive pre-coded in claims systems. I could not retrieve the 고시 text and my web search budget was exhausted (200/200) before I located a primary URL, so I have deliberately excluded it from the findings. This should be the first item in any follow-up.

domains.newHypotheses:
1. SUBSTRATE-AVAILABILITY BEATS MONEY-PROXIMITY. Replace the guideline -> CDS -> measure -> rating -> payment gradient with a single binary: does the data stream the instrument reads at the moment it fires carry a diagnosis? Retrospective instruments reading medical claims or EHR records (HEDIS, CMS506v7) retain axis B regardless of whether money is attached. Real-time instruments firing inside a pharmacy dispensing transaction (Medicare Part D POS edits, Korea's DUR and the NIMS narcotics dispensing-history lookup) lose it, because NCPDP-style pharmacy transactions carry drug, quantity, days supply and patient identifiers but no diagnosis. Aggregate prescribing datasets with no patient linkage at all (English practice-level prescribing data) cannot carry it under any circumstances. This variable is confounded with money-proximity in the PIM prior — payment instruments there also happened to be transactional — and it comes apart cleanly in opioid safety, where the most payment-linked instrument (CMS506v7) has the richest binding and the most transactional one (Part D POS) has none. This hypothesis is directly testable: find a retrospective payment instrument (a claims-based value-based-payment measure) and a non-payment real-time instrument (a pure EHR alert), and check which axis survives.

2. THE DIRECTIONAL ASYMMETRY: EXCULPATORY CONDITIONS SURVIVE, INCULPATORY CONDITIONS DO NOT. Add a third axis to the taxonomy. Axis B splits into B-exclusion (condition removes a patient from the measure: cancer, sickle cell, hospice, palliative care, OUD) and B-trigger (condition makes the prescription hazardous: sleep-disordered breathing, prior overdose, renal/hepatic insufficiency). In opioid safety, B-exclusion survives in every US instrument I read and B-trigger survives in none. The likely driver is accountability structure, not terminology: an unbound exclusion produces a specific harmed patient who can file a coverage appeal and whose clinician will complain, so the operating body bears a concentrated cost and pays to bind it; an unbound trigger produces only a diffuse statistical harm with no complainant, so nobody bears a cost and nobody binds it. This predicts that B-exclusion should be well bound and B-trigger poorly bound ACROSS domains, and it would reframe the PIM finding too — I would expect Korea's 2022 criteria and Japan's deleted 'target patient group' column to be B-trigger losses specifically, and I would predict that if any of those instruments has an exemption for palliative or cancer patients, that exemption IS bound. Worth re-examining the PIM data along this split.

3. RULE SHAPE MAY BE UPSTREAM OF BOTH. In opioid safety the consensus itself put its authority into a QUANTITATIVE DOSE THRESHOLD (50 and 90 MME) and a DRUG-DRUG PAIR, both computable from dispensing alone, and left the drug-disease content as unnumbered prose. In the PIM domain the consensus put its authority into an enumerated drug list plus an enumerated drug-disease table. If consensus panels systematically place their most operationalisable content in the most operationalisable shape, then part of what looks like differential SURVIVAL is actually differential SPECIFICATION EFFORT at the consensus stage. Testable by measuring, in each consensus source, the ratio of quantified/enumerated statements to prose statements on each axis, and checking whether that ratio predicts downstream survival better than binding authorship does.

4. NAMED-BUT-UNBOUND IS A DISTINCT THIRD STATE AND SHOULD BE CODED SEPARATELY. The Part D POS edit is neither 'axis retained' nor 'axis dropped'. CMS names five exempt populations and then delegates the definition entirely. The observable consequence is heterogeneous implementation across sponsors and an exemption that depends on pharmacist recall. The current retained/dropped binary hides this state, and it is probably common — it is the cheapest way for an agency to appear to preserve clinical nuance without paying for it. Recommend recoding every instrument in the study as retained-and-bound / retained-but-unbound / dropped / never-present.

verdict.reasoning: CLAIM 1 — MIXED, and the domain forces a restatement. This domain is a degenerate case for the asymmetry test because the consensus criteria are essentially 100% condition-dependent: STOPP v3 Section E is 10/10 drug-x-eGFR criteria, Beers Table 6 is 24/24 drug-x-CrCl entries, and Beers' drug-disease table (Table 3) contains no kidney row at all. There is no drug-only axis in the source to survive preferentially, so the naive form of Claim 1 cannot be scored. What I found instead is a sharper and, I think, more informative phenomenon: where axis B was lost, the operating body did not drop the clinical topic — it MANUFACTURED a drug-only surrogate to carry it. NHS BSA replaced 'NSAID in renal impairment' with AKI01, a pure NSAID+RAS+diuretic triple. Scotland's Appendix E replaced 'metformin if eGFR<30' with 'metformin and ACEI/ARB and NSAID'. Japan replaced the threshold table with a bare two-column list of renally-excreted drug names. In all three, a condition-dependent criterion was converted into a drug-only one. That is strong support for the SPIRIT of Claim 1 (drug-only content is what national instruments can hold) while contradicting its letter (axis B was not lost by attrition; it was actively re-encoded). Set against this, axis B was retained outright in 5 of the 13 instruments I examined, across 4 jurisdictions — a substantially higher survival rate than the PIM prior would predict, which is why I score this mixed rather than supported. CLAIM 2 — SUPPORTED, strongly and without exception in my sample. Every single retention has an identifiable authored binding applied inside the indicator definition: PRIMIS authored the EGFR_COD SNOMED cluster and PINCER indicator K tests it against eGFR<45; NHS Digital named ORALNSAIDDRUG_COD/CKD_COD/EGFR_COD and NICE IND232 applies them; AWTTC authored an operational definition combining CKD-register membership with numeric thresholds (<59, <45) over DHCW GP data; KNMP authored the standard clearance cut-offs (80/50/30/10 to 90/60/30/15 from January 2026) inside the G-Standaard and the Dutch CKD guideline mandates that the eGFR be transmitted to the pharmacist so the binding can fire; NCQA authored five value sets (ESRD Diagnosis, CKD Stage 4, Dialysis Procedure, Total Nephrectomy, Kidney Transplant). And every loss has no binding AND, decisively, no access to the substrate: NHS BSA, Scotland's PIS-based indicators and PHS's NTIs all run on prescribed-and-reimbursed data; Korea's DUR runs on the prescription plus the resident registration number. Korea is the cleanest confirmation available anywhere in this study: all nine surviving DUR categories are exactly those computable from prescription+RRN, and the renal axis — which is not — is absent. However, the domain requires one substantive AMENDMENT to the stated mechanism. The hypothesis reasons that 'drugs arrive pre-coded as a by-product of dispensing/claiming; conditions do not'. In primary-care EHR systems that is false for this condition: eGFR arrives pre-coded and automatically with every U&E result, and is a single numeric field. This is why England, Wales and the Netherlands could bind the LAB VALUE directly and did so, achieving something they could not achieve for a diagnosis-defined condition. Conversely NCQA, working from claims, found the DIAGNOSIS pre-coded and the lab unusable — its spec literally instructs 'Do not include laboratory claims (claims with POS code 81)'. So the correct mechanism is not drug-versus-condition; it is SUBSTRATE VISIBILITY. Axis B survives where the operating body's pipeline contains the substrate the condition is written in, and bodies rewrite the condition into whichever substrate they can see. CLAIM 3 — SUPPORTED, with an explicit caveat that the payment layer is only partly assessable. Retention by layer in my sample: guideline 3/4 retained (Scotland guidance, Netherlands CNS richtlijn, and the consensus sources; Japan's MHLW national guideline LOST it); decision-support 2/3 retained (England PINCER, Netherlands G-Standaard; Korea DUR LOST it); measure-specification 2/5 retained (Wales, NICE IND232 in transformed form; NHS BSA, Scotland Appendix E and PHS NTI all LOST it); public-rating 1/1 retained (NCQA DDE, diagnosis-bound); payment 0/2 retained. I found NO instrument in any jurisdiction, at the payment layer, that conditions a drug rule on kidney function. NICE's own validity assessment states that QOF contained 'a single indicator for CKD', which is a register/detection indicator rather than a drug rule. Korea's DUR, which does carry reimbursement consequences via 심사조정, has no renal category. And the crispest observation I obtained is Wales's within-instrument gradient: the condition-dependent Prescribing Safety Indicators carry 'Target for 2025-2026: No target set', while the drug-volume indicator on the very next page carries a hard numeric target of 1,165 ADQs per 1,000 STAR-PUs. That suggests the gradient may operate not by deleting axis-B indicators near money but by measuring them without attaching money to them. Caveat: I could not read CMS Star Ratings or MIPS specifications (both cms.gov endpoints returned 403/Access Denied), and I could not read Korea's 약제급여기준 고시 or Japan's 診療報酬/調剤報酬 schedules, where drug-specific reimbursement conditions keyed to creatinine clearance are plausible. My payment-layer verdict rests on England, Wales and Korea only.

domains.contradictions: I searched deliberately for refutations and found five that matter. (1) THE CENTRAL MECHANISM AS STATED IS WRONG FOR THIS DOMAIN. The hypothesis says conditions fail to survive because 'drugs arrive pre-coded as a by-product of dispensing/claiming; conditions do not.' In primary-care EHR systems eGFR also arrives pre-coded, automatically, as a numeric field on every U&E result — it needs no clinician to remember to code it, unlike a diagnosis. That is precisely why three national instruments bound the LAB VALUE directly and successfully: PINCER indicator K ('Patients aged >=18 years with chronic renal failure: eGFR <45 mL/min at least 3 months before the audit date'), Wales ('have an eGFR of < 59 ml/min', and nitrofurantoin at '< 45 ml/min'), and the KNMP G-Standaard (cut-offs moving to 90/60/30/15 ml/min in January 2026). A lab-value condition is not harder to bind than a diagnosis; in EHR-based systems it is easier. The domain therefore refutes the drug-vs-condition framing and supports a substrate-visibility framing instead. (2) THE SUBSTITUTION RUNS THE OPPOSITE WAY IN THE US. NCQA took a criterion that is a LAB THRESHOLD in the source (Beers Table 6: NSAIDs, avoid if CrCl <30) and operationalized it with DIAGNOSIS AND PROCEDURE value sets (CKD Stage 4, ESRD, dialysis, nephrectomy, transplant), while explicitly instructing 'Do not include laboratory claims (claims with POS code 81)'. For a claims-based body the diagnosis is the pre-coded thing and the lab is invisible — the exact inverse of the hypothesis's premise. Any general statement of the mechanism must be substrate-relative, not condition-relative. (3) AXIS B SURVIVED FAR MORE OFTEN THAN THE PIM PRIOR PREDICTS. The prior reports Korea adopting 0% of the condition axis and retention of 1/3 at rating and 0/4 at payment. Here axis B was retained in 5 of 13 national instruments across England, Wales, the Netherlands and the US, including at the public-rating layer (NCQA DDE, live in HEDIS MY2026). The Netherlands is a particularly hard case for the pessimistic reading: it did not merely author a binding, it built national infrastructure to carry the lab value to the dispenser ('Een bekende verminderde nierfunctie (< 50 ml/min/1,73 m2) moet door de voorschrijver worden doorgegeven aan de apotheker'). (4) 'RETAINED' AND 'LOST' ARE NOT EXHAUSTIVE — I FOUND AT LEAST TWO OTHER FATES. NICE IND232 retained the condition axis but MUTATED the criterion from a contraindication into a monitoring indicator: EGFR_COD is used only to detect that a test happened, never to test the threshold, and CKD_COD appears only as a denominator exclusion. Japan's MHLW retained the axis as a METHOD rather than a rule: 別表3 has only '薬効分類 | 薬物名' columns and no threshold, while 別紙 supplies the Giusti-Hayton correction factor for the clinician to compute. Neither is captured by a binary retained/lost coding, and both would be miscoded by an automated pass. (5) THE CONSENSUS SOURCES DISAGREE WITH THEMSELVES, WHICH IS AN ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION FOR NON-ADOPTION AT PAYMENT. For the single most-operationalized criterion in the domain — NSAIDs in renal impairment — the thresholds are Beers CrCl <30, STOPP v3 eGFR <50, PINCER eGFR <45, Wales eGFR <59, NCQA CKD Stage 4 (i.e. <30). That is a two-fold spread. Attrition near payment may be driven by threshold non-convergence rather than by codeability, and my data cannot separate the two. Relatedly, the STOPP v3 panel itself REJECTED the ACEi and ARB eGFR<30 criteria (main paper Table 2), so condition-axis attrition begins inside the consensus process before any national body is involved. Finally, one non-contradiction worth flagging so it is not miscounted as one: KDIGO 2024 Chapter 4 has no enumerated drug-x-threshold list at all — only prose practice points and zero codes. That is case (a) in your taxonomy, not a dropped axis, and the hypothesis has nothing to bite on there.

domains.newHypotheses: H1 — SUBSTRATE VISIBILITY (replaces the drug-vs-condition mechanism). Axis B survives if and only if the operating body's data pipeline physically contains the substrate in which the condition is expressed, and the body authors a binding into THAT substrate. It is not that conditions are intrinsically harder to code than drugs; it is that each body can see some substrates and not others. EHR-based bodies (PINCER, AWTTC, KNMP) saw the lab and bound the lab value. The claims-based body (NCQA) could not see the lab, saw the diagnosis, and bound the diagnosis — accepting a large sensitivity loss, since CKD Stage 4/ESRD codes capture only diagnosed and coded severe disease. Dispensing-only bodies (NHS BSA, Scotland PIS, Korea DUR) saw neither and dropped it. This predicts, testably, that the same clinical criterion will be bound to different substrates in different countries as a pure function of data architecture, and that the retained thresholds will drift apart accordingly — which is exactly the two-fold NSAID threshold spread I observed (<30 to <59). H2 — SURROGATE SUBSTITUTION, NOT DELETION. Where the substrate is invisible, national bodies do not abandon the clinical topic; they synthesize a drug-only proxy that approximates it using only what they can see. Evidence: NHS BSA's AKI01 (NSAID+RAS+diuretic), Scotland's 'metformin and ACEI/ARB and NSAID' standing in for 'metformin if eGFR<30', Japan's bare renally-excreted drug list. This means studies that code criteria as retained/lost will systematically undercount, because the topic survives while the axis does not. It also predicts that the 'triple whammy' construct — which has no basis in any consensus criteria set I read — is an artefact of dispensing-data architecture rather than a clinical finding, and should be over-represented in exactly those countries whose national indicators run on reimbursement data. H3 — EVENT-BINDING IS CHEAPER THAN VALUE-BINDING. Binding a lab EVENT (a coded test result exists) requires only a code cluster; binding a lab VALUE requires the numeric result plus an agreed threshold plus a defensible time window. NICE IND232 is a clean instance of a body choosing the cheap version and thereby converting a contraindication into a monitoring indicator. Prediction: as instruments move toward payment, condition-dependent criteria will preferentially appear in the monitoring form ('was a test done') rather than the threshold form ('was the drug given below X'), because the monitoring form is auditable and uncontested. H4 — TARGET EXEMPTION AS THE REAL PAYMENT GRADIENT. The gradient may not operate by deleting axis-B indicators near money but by measuring them without money attached. Wales measures its condition-dependent safety indicators nationally and states 'Target for 2025-2026: No target set', while attaching a hard numeric target to the drug-volume indicator on the facing page. This is directly testable across instruments: code each indicator for (condition-dependent y/n) and (carries a numeric target y/n) and test for association. If H4 holds it is a more precise statement of Claim 3 than 'axis B is lost near payment'. H5 — THRESHOLD NON-CONVERGENCE AS AN INDEPENDENT BARRIER. A payer cannot attach money to a number that the consensus bodies disagree about by a factor of two. Where consensus sources converge on a single threshold, axis B should reach payment; where they diverge, it should stall at measurement regardless of how codeable it is. This is a rival explanation to the codeability mechanism for the payment-layer findings and my data cannot distinguish them; it should be tested in a domain (e.g. anticoagulant dosing in AF, where CrCl thresholds are label-fixed and therefore convergent) where the two mechanisms make opposite predictions.

verdict.reasoning:
COUNTS. Of the 15 national instruments I could classify (excluding the two marked unassessable/null), the condition axis was RETAINED in 11 and ABSENT in 4. By layer: guideline 1/1 retained; measure-specification 5/6 retained (ECDC the sole loss); public-rating 2/2 retained; payment 5/7 retained (England's Quality Premium and Japan's 抗菌薬適正使用体制加算 the two losses). There is no monotonic decay toward money.

CLAIM 1 — CONTRADICTED. In antimicrobial stewardship the condition axis is not a modifier bolted onto a drug rule; it IS the criterion. 'Antibiotic for acute bronchitis' has no drug-only residue — strip the condition and there is no measure left, only a volume count. Korea, the USA and Japan all operationalised the condition axis into national instruments, and Korea ADDED a second condition-dependent indicator (급성하기도감염 J20-J22) in 2020. The drug-only axis dominates in exactly two places, England and ECDC, and both documents state the reason on their face: the data substrate is a prescribing/consumption feed (NHSBSA ePACT; ATC/DDD sales) that contains no diagnosis field at all.

CLAIM 2 — MIXED, and the stated mechanism is wrong in its 'only' form. SUPPORTED where the instrument computes a rate from claims: HIRA wrote KCD J00–J06 into the indicator definition; NCQA wrote the Acute Bronchitis / Comorbid Conditions / Competing Diagnosis / Pharyngitis Value Sets in ICD-10-CM and SNOMED and CMS adopted them intact; MHLW wrote ICD-10 J00–J06 and A00–A09 into its guideline footnotes. CONTRADICTED in four instruments where the condition axis survives with NO authored diagnosis code list: Japan's 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 pays 80 points on the natural-language conditions 急性気道感染症・急性中耳炎・急性副鼻腔炎; Japan's 感染対策向上加算１ AST duty names 急性気道感染症 and 急性下痢症 with no codes; England's Pharmacy First pays a fee only when a condition-specific 'gateway point' is crossed, bound by a clinical algorithm (FeverPAIN) rather than a code list; Australia's PBS gates reimbursement on a structured 'Indication:' restriction. So an authored code list is SUFFICIENT for survival but not NECESSARY. Two substitutes work: an authored operational clinical algorithm, and adjudication against a diagnosis field the payer already mandates on every claim.

Also false is the premise behind Claim 2 — 'Drugs arrive pre-coded as a by-product of dispensing/claiming; conditions do not.' In fee-for-service claims systems conditions ALSO arrive pre-coded as a by-product of claiming: Korea requires KCD on every 명세서, Japan requires 傷病名 on every receipt, the USA requires ICD-10-CM on every claim. That is precisely where the condition axis survived. Where it died, England and ECDC, the operating body's feed was a prescription/sales extract with no diagnosis at all. The real constraint is substrate, not authorship.

CLAIM 3 — CONTRADICTED, with a hint of the reverse gradient. Four separate payment-layer instruments in three jurisdictions retain the condition axis: Korea's 가감지급사업 adjusts payment by up to ±5% on the J00–J06 antibiotic rate; Japan pays 80 points per encounter for NOT prescribing in a named condition; England pays a Pharmacy First consultation fee only on a condition-specific gateway; Australia's PBS makes the subsidy itself conditional on the indication. Money-proximity did not strip the condition axis — arguably it protected it, because a payer that already adjudicates claims by diagnosis has the diagnosis in hand and can enforce on it. The two payment instruments that ARE drug-only (England's Quality Premium, Japan's AWaRe-Access add-on) are drug-only for a data reason, not a money reason: they are computed over prescribing/consumption feeds, not over claims.

domains.contradictions:
Six concrete cases that argue against the hypothesis, all read in primary documents:

(1) KOREA, PAYMENT LAYER, CONDITION AXIS SURVIVES (vs Claim 3 and Claim 1). HIRA's 가감지급사업 pays or claws back up to 5% on 급성상기도감염 항생제처방률, an indicator whose definition is verbatim '급성상기도감염(J00-J06) 상병의 항생제 처방 빈도를 나타내는 지표'. The diagnosis code range is in the indicator name, in the graded public disclosure, and in the money. HIRA report 2024.7 p.2: '2017년: 급성상기도감염 항생제처방률 가감지급 모형개선(’18년 심사결정분) - 상대평가→절대평가(목표치 제시), 가감률 확대(1%→최대 5%)'.

(2) JAPAN, PAYMENT LAYER, CONDITION AXIS SURVIVES WITHOUT ANY CODE LIST (vs Claims 2 and 3). '耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 80点（月１回に限り）... 急性気道感染症、急性中耳炎又は急性副鼻腔炎により受診した６歳未満の乳幼児に対して ... 抗菌薬の投与の必要性が認められないため抗菌薬を使用しない場合において'. MHLW authored no ICD binding here; the condition is a plain disease name adjudicated against the receipt's mandatory 傷病名 field.

(3) AUSTRALIA, THE MONEY ITSELF IS CONDITION-GATED (vs Claim 3). PBS norfloxacin 3010K: 'Authority Required / Restriction Indication: Acute bacterial enterocolitis / Restriction Indication: Complicated urinary tract infection'. Reimbursement does not exist outside the indication.

(4) ENGLAND, PAYMENT LAYER, CONDITION AXIS SURVIVES VIA AN ALGORITHM NOT A CODE LIST (vs Claims 2 and 3). Pharmacy First: seven named conditions, and 'a fee is payable only when a gateway point [is crossed]', with the sore-throat gateway defined by 'Use FeverPAIN Score to assess'. England, the jurisdiction that produced the cleanest drug-only payment instrument in 2015, produced a condition-dependent one in 2023.

(5) JAPAN'S NATIONAL GUIDELINE AUTHORED ICD CODES FOR ITS CONDITIONS (vs the PIM-domain premise that consensus sources specify zero diagnosis codes). 注4: '国際疾病分類第 10 版(ICD10)において J00～J06 に分類される疾病。' 注12: 'ICD10 コードにおいて A00～A09 をまとめたもの。' In the PIM domain, MHLW deleted the target-patient-group column; in this domain, MHLW coded it.

(6) THE COMORBIDITY AXIS — the exact thing lost in the PIM domain — IS RETAINED AND CODED IN THE US MEASURE. Cases I actively searched for that WOULD have supported the hypothesis, and what I found: I looked for a national antibiotic indicator that started condition-specific and was narrowed to drug-only on adoption. I did not find one. The closest is the removal of the URI and Pharyngitis measures from the 2025 Medicaid Child Core Set (they are absent from the manual I read, where a 'Pharyngitis Value Set' survives only inside AAB-CH) — but AAB, equally condition-dependent, was retained, so this looks like set parsimony rather than an axis failure, and I could not verify CMS's stated reason. The genuine drug-only instruments (England's Quality Premium, ECDC ESAC-Net, Japan's AWaRe-Access add-on) never had a condition axis to lose: they were built on prescribing/consumption feeds that never carried a diagnosis.

domains.newHypotheses:
Two replacements, both better fits to what I read than the Binding-Survival Hypothesis.

A. SUBSTRATE HYPOTHESIS (replaces Claim 2's mechanism). The condition axis survives operationalization iff the data feed the instrument runs on already carries a diagnosis field, for reasons unrelated to the indicator. It is not that drugs are pre-coded and conditions are not — in every fee-for-service claims system, conditions are pre-coded too, because the payer will not adjudicate a claim without a diagnosis (KCD in Korea, 傷病名 in Japan, ICD-10-CM in the US). What varies is which feed the operating body chose. Korea, Japan and the US compute antibiotic indicators over claims, which carry both drug and diagnosis; England's Quality Premium and ECDC's ESAC-Net compute over NHSBSA prescription extracts and ATC/DDD consumption data, which carry drug only. Predicted test: any national antibiotic indicator built on a dispensing-only or sales-only feed will be drug-only regardless of layer, and any built on a claims feed will retain the condition axis regardless of layer. That holds for all 15 instruments here without exception. It also retro-explains the PIM result: England's PINCER ran on GP EHR records (diagnoses present, Read codes authored) and retained the axis; the instruments that lost it were the ones running on prescription data.

B. SEVERABILITY HYPOTHESIS (replaces Claim 1). The condition axis survives when it is constitutive of the criterion and is dropped when it is a severable modifier. In PIM criteria the structure is 'avoid drug X [, if condition Y]' — deleting the bracket leaves a working drug-only rule, so the bracket is cheap to drop. In antimicrobial stewardship the structure is 'for condition Y, do not use antibiotics' — deleting the condition leaves nothing measurable, so it cannot be dropped. This predicts that the asymmetry reported in the PIM domain is a property of criterion GRAMMAR, not of drug-versus-condition ontology, and would reverse in any domain where the condition is the subject rather than the qualifier. Discriminating test against hypothesis A: find a claims-based national instrument with a severable condition modifier (e.g. Korea's own 노인주의 의약품 처방률, which HIRA runs on the same claims feed as the antibiotic indicators but which I saw specified as drug-only in the 2023 report). If severable modifiers are dropped even on a diagnosis-rich substrate, B dominates A; if HIRA codes them when it wants to, A dominates.

C. Minor: a THIRD binding type deserves its own category alongside code lists and operational definitions — the 'adjudicated natural-language indication' (Japan's fee add-ons, Australia's PBS restrictions). It is not a terminology binding at all; enforcement is retrospective audit against a field the claim already carries. It is the cheapest way to keep a condition axis and it appears only in payment instruments, which is the opposite of what Claim 3 predicts.

domains.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia (older adults; nursing home / long-term care and community)

verdict.reasoning:
CLAIM 1 (mixed, leaning weakly supported). The drug axis survived in 11 of 11 national instruments I verified: every one of them carries a fully enumerated drug binding (NDC lists, HCPCS lists, MDS N0415A/N0410A items, BNF prescribing data, or a 16-ingredient Korean ingredient list). But the condition axis survived in 8 of 11 - far more often than the 0% adoption rate seen in the Korean PIM prior. So the asymmetry is real but MUCH weaker in this domain. Two reasons, both of which qualify the claim. (a) In this domain the criterion is condition-dependent by construction, so an instrument that dropped the condition axis entirely would not be recognisable as operationalising the criterion at all; the surviving instruments had to keep something. (b) Crucially, what survived is usually NOT the criterion's index condition. CMS N047.01, CMS N011.03 and CIHI all dropped DEMENTIA from the denominator and kept only the FDA-approved-indication exclusion set (schizophrenia, bipolar, Huntington's, Tourette's, psychosis). Only PQA/CMS APD (display) and NICE IND12 (network-level) retained dementia as the index condition. Counted at the level of the index condition, the asymmetry looks much closer to the PIM prior: index-condition retention is 2 of 11.

CLAIM 2 (supported). The split is clean. Every instrument that retained a computable condition axis has an authored, applied binding: CMS authored MDS Section I item codes and, from V18.0, a 14-code ICD-10 exclusion list applied against Medicare/Medicaid claims; PQA authored 114 ICD-10 codes (40 dementia, 62 approved-indication, 12 major depression) and CMS applies them against CWF and EDS; CIHI authored RAI-MDS 2.0 / interRAI item codes plus ICD-10 G10 and G3080. Every instrument that lost the condition axis had no condition binding and substituted a proxy that arrives pre-coded: Scotland substituted an age threshold and care-home residency; Korea substituted nothing at all and used principal diagnosis only as a case-mix adjuster inside a Prescription Index; Japan substituted drug counts. The Korean case is a near-perfect replication of the prior PIM finding: HIRA authored KCD codes for neighbouring conditions on its own patient assessment form (헌팅톤병 G10, 파킨슨병 G20, 다발경화증 G35 - including the very Huntington's code that CMS and CIHI use as an exclusion), left dementia uncoded, and applied none of them in the criterion. The one real counterexample is 42 CFR 483.45(e)/F758, where the condition axis survives with NO terminology binding whatsoever - only the narrative rule 'a specific condition as diagnosed and documented in the clinical record'. That works because the instrument is adjudicated by human surveyors reading charts, not computed from claims. So Claim 2 should be narrowed to: a CODED binding is necessary for a condition axis to survive into a COMPUTED indicator; instruments adjudicated by inspection can carry a condition axis on a narrative operational definition instead.

CLAIM 3 (mixed). There is a real signal at the money end but the gradient is not monotonic and is broken at both ends. Retention by layer among instruments I verified: guideline/consensus 5 of 5 (FDA label, NG97, Beers, PQA, Korean handbook - all condition-dependent); measure-specification 3 of 4 (APD, IND12, Australia retained; Scotland lost); public-rating 3 of 3 (CMS long-stay, CMS short-stay, CIHI - all retained, all code-bound); payment 1 of 3 retained (F758 retained; Korea HIRA lost; Japan lost), plus one layer where the whole criterion is simply absent (Part D Star Ratings). Supporting evidence for the gradient: the single most completely condition-bound instrument in the domain, PQA/CMS APD, has never been promoted from the display page to the Star Ratings, and the CY2026 memo confirms its long-term-nursing-home variant is being retired from the display page altogether; and Korea's payment-linked indicator is the one that stripped the condition axis to a pure drug rate while keeping the payment consequence (20% inpatient-fee bonus, 5%-bottom penalty). Contradicting evidence: Scotland lost the condition axis at a purely quality-improvement layer with no money attached at all, and the United States RETAINS the condition axis in a payment-enforcement regulation (F758) whose remedies under 42 CFR 488.406 include denial of payment for new admissions and civil money penalties. The gradient is therefore better described as a gradient in the DATA-COMPUTABILITY of the instrument than in its distance from money: instruments computed automatically from administrative claims lose the condition axis unless someone paid to author a code list, regardless of whether they pay out.

domains.contradictions:
Four substantive contradictions found, plus one mechanism-level complication.

1. CONTRADICTS CLAIM 3 - condition axis retained AT the payment layer. 42 CFR 483.45(e), survey tag F758, requires that psychotropics not be given "unless the medication is necessary to treat a specific condition as diagnosed and documented in the clinical record", and non-compliance triggers denial of payment for new admissions and civil money penalties (42 CFR 488.406, verified at eCFR). This is as close to money as any instrument in the domain and the condition axis is fully present.

2. CONTRADICTS CLAIM 2 (narrow reading) - condition axis survived with NO terminology binding. The same F758 carries no value set, no code list, no ICD/SNOMED mapping. The binding is a narrative rule enforced by human surveyors reading charts. Terminology bindings turn out to be necessary for COMPUTED indicators, not for condition axes in general.

3. CONTRADICTS CLAIM 3 - condition axis lost FAR from money. Public Health Scotland's National Therapeutic Indicators are a pure quality-improvement instrument with no payment attached, and across all 139 indicators there is not one mention of dementia. The three antipsychotic indicators are drug-plus-age (NTI 8e/8ea: ">=75 years prescribed an antipsychotic as a percentage of all people aged >=75 years"), drug-plus-care-home-residency (CHNTI 8ea), and drug-plus-drug (NTI 8pf). Distance from money did not protect the condition axis here.

4. CONTRADICTS THE PRIOR-DOMAIN GENERALISATION that consensus sources never specify codes. PQA, a consensus measure-development body, authored the diagnosis code lists itself as part of the criterion (Table Dementia A, Table Dementia D in the 2015 specification; 114 ICD-10 codes in the current value-set workbook). This is the one consensus source in the set that did not leave the condition uncoded, and it is precisely the source whose condition axis survived intact into a national instrument. That is confirmatory for the mechanism but refutes any blanket claim that consensus bodies do not author bindings.

5. MECHANISM COMPLICATION - the binding is necessary but not sufficient, and becomes an attack surface. CMS's own guidance states verbatim: "CMS is aware of situations where practitioners have potentially misdiagnosed residents with a condition for which antipsychotics are an approved use (e.g., new diagnosis of schizophrenia) which would then exclude the resident from the long-stay antipsychotic quality measure." CMS's response was to strengthen the binding: the V18.0 re-specification effective 2026-01-01 now requires the schizophrenia/Tourette's/Huntington's exclusion to be corroborated by an ICD-10 code in Medicare/Medicaid claims within a defined lookback window, not merely asserted on the MDS. So authoring a binding does not end the story; once the binding gates a public rating, it is gamed, and the operating body has to re-author it against a second data source.

Things I actively looked for that would have refuted the hypothesis but did NOT find: a national payment instrument in Korea or Japan that carries a dementia-bound antipsychotic criterion (none found); a condition-bound antipsychotic indicator in Scotland's NTI set (none, across all 139 rows); a Star Ratings (payment-linked) version of APD (none - explicitly display-only).

domains.newHypotheses:
Three refinements my domain suggests, all grounded in the verified documents.

H1 - THE INDICATION-CARVE-OUT ASYMMETRY (a split inside axis B). Axis B is not one thing. It has two sub-axes that behave completely differently under operationalisation:
  B-index: the condition that makes the drug risky (dementia).
  B-carveout: the conditions that make the drug legitimate (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, Huntington's disease, Tourette's syndrome, psychosis).
In this domain B-carveout survived almost everywhere it mattered (CMS long-stay, CMS short-stay, CIHI, PQA/CMS APD) while B-index was dropped by CMS and CIHI and retained only by PQA/APD and NICE IND12. The mechanism is the same data economics that the hypothesis identifies for drugs: B-carveout conditions are the FDA-approved indications, so they are already adjudicated and coded in claims BECAUSE the payer needed them to reimburse the antipsychotic. B-index conditions have no such reimbursement-driven coding pressure. The Beers Table 2 drug-only row makes this visible in the source itself - "Avoid, except in FDA-approved indications such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, Parkinson disease psychosis..." - the carve-out list arrives attached to the DRUG entry, not the disease entry, and it is exactly that list which CMS and PQA coded. Prediction: across other domains, the sub-axis of axis B that names an approved indication for the same drug will survive operationalisation at roughly the drug axis's rate, while the sub-axis naming a contraindication or risk state will survive at the low rate the PIM prior observed.

H2 - PROXY SUBSTITUTION RATHER THAN SIMPLE DELETION. Where axis B was lost, it was not left blank; it was replaced by whichever variable is already coded in the same data stream. Scotland substituted age (>=75) and care-home residency for dementia. CMS and CIHI substituted long-stay nursing-home residency for dementia. Korea substituted the long-term-care-hospital inpatient setting, and used principal diagnosis only as a case-mix adjuster inside a Prescription Index. Japan substituted drug counts. This is a more informative description than "axis B was lost": operationalisation trades a clinical condition for the cheapest available correlate of that condition. It also explains why nobody notices the loss - the resulting indicator still looks like it is about dementia patients.

H3 - COMPUTABILITY, NOT PROXIMITY TO MONEY, IS THE ACTIVE VARIABLE. F758 (payment-enforcement, condition axis retained, no codes) and Scotland's NTIs (no money, condition axis lost) together break the money gradient. What separates them is how the indicator is adjudicated. Human-adjudicated instruments (chart review by surveyors) can carry a condition axis on narrative language because a human supplies the mapping at inspection time. Machine-computed instruments cannot, and so require someone to fund and maintain a code list. Restating Claim 3 this way also predicts the direction of drift over time: as instruments are automated for scale, condition axes that were carried narratively will be lost unless a binding is authored at the moment of automation - and the CMS V18.0 re-specification, which had to add a claims-based ICD-10 confirmation to a binding that was previously carried by a single MDS checkbox, is exactly that moment happening.

domains.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review (SMR) targeting, deprescribing indicators, drug-count thresholds, and polypharmacy case-finding. Jurisdictions reached: Japan (MHLW shinryo-hoshu + chozai-hoshu), England (NICE, NHS England PCN DES/IIF, NHSBSA), Scotland (Scottish Government/NHS Scotland Polypharmacy Guidance, STU/RDS, National Therapeutic Indicators), USA (42 CFR Part D MTM, CMS Star Ratings, PQA/CMS Patient Safety measures), Korea (MFDS DUR designation rule, NHIS polypharmacy management programme, HIRA P4P framework).

verdict.reasoning:
CLAIM 1 (asymmetry) - SUPPORTED, and the domain provides an unusually clean quantification. In every consensus source I read from the primary document, a condition-dependent axis exists: Scotland 42 of 69 case-finding indicators 'utilise diagnosis, examination signs and laboratory data'; NICE NG5 names 'chronic or long-term conditions'; MHLW's guideline builds its whole review flowchart on comorbidity, renal function and nutritional state. In every nationally COMPUTED instrument I could read, the surviving criterion is a drug count or a drug-drug combination plus an age band. Japan's three polypharmacy fees are 6-or-more oral drugs reduced by 2-or-more, with no diagnosis element and, tellingly, a new structured claim field created for the drug count and none for any condition. England's four money-bearing SMR-02 indicators are drug-drug pairs plus age. NHSBSA's national polypharmacy comparators (v2.2.0, May 2026) are defined entirely on BNF codes and age bands. Scotland's own National Therapeutic Indicators contain zero diagnosis criteria. Korea's national DUR regulation enumerates nine check categories and none is diagnosis-based. The domain also shows the substitution mechanism directly, twice in writing: NHSBSA encodes 'does not have hypertension' as 'not prescribed an antihypertensive', and Scotland encodes 'has diabetes' as 'prescribed an anti-diabetic drug'.

CLAIM 2 (binding mechanism) - MIXED, and I think the claim needs one amendment. The positive evidence is strong. Scotland is the cleanest confirmation available anywhere in this domain: NHS National Services Scotland authored a Read-to-SNOMED plus DM&D specification for every case-finding indicator, stored it in EScro, ran it nightly against every primary care record, and applied it in both STU reports and Right Decision Service alerts - and the condition axis survived intact, including dementia, oestrogen-dependent cancer, and diagnosed asthma without COPD. England supplies a near-experimental control inside a single payment document: in the same Annex B, same layer, same GPES data source, the two indicators denominated on the QOF Asthma Register (a pre-existing SNOMED-backed disease register) reached payment with full thresholds and real money, while the polypharmacy/SMR content, which had no equivalent register, reached payment as drug-drug pairs only, and the one condition-referencing indicator (SMR-01) had its thresholds left 'TBC'. Korea's DUR shows the negative case: no diagnosis binding was ever authored, and the national CDS has no condition axis at all.

But US Part D MTM contradicts the claim as literally worded. 42 CFR 423.153(d)(2) is a payment-layer requirement whose condition axis not only survived but was STRENGTHENED effective 1 January 2025, when CMS moved from sponsor discretion to a mandatory list of ten named chronic diseases - with no ICD-10 codes, no value set, and no named code authority. The amendment I would propose is that a condition axis survives national operationalization by one of two routes, not one: (a) the operating body authors and applies a binding, which yields a nationally computable and comparable indicator (Scotland, England's QOF-backed indicators); or (b) the operating body delegates both the definition and the measurement to the reporting entity, which yields a requirement that is enforceable but not comparable. CMS took route (b), and the fingerprint is visible in the Star Ratings measure that scores it: D11's denominator is 'those beneficiaries who meet the contracts' specified targeting criteria', and its data source is 'Part D Plan Reporting' - plan self-report - whereas the drug-count polypharmacy measures in the same programme are computed centrally by CMS from PDE claims using PQA value sets. Route (b) is available only where no cross-entity comparison of the condition itself is required. Note also that the mechanism's premise is confirmed word-for-word inside a single regulatory paragraph: for the drug count CMS says sponsors must rely 'on information in a widely accepted, commercially or publicly available drug database', and for the ten diseases it says nothing at all.

CLAIM 3 (gradient toward payment) - MIXED, leaning supported, with one real contradiction. Three within-jurisdiction gradients support it, and within-jurisdiction comparisons are the strongest design available because they hold the health system constant. Scotland: the same 2026-2029 guidance carries the full condition-and-lab indicator set into the practice-level CDS and a condition-free, drug-proxied set into the national benchmarking layer, and the 2018 edition states the loss in its own words - the 42 diagnosis/lab indicators 'cannot be straightforwardly used to identify prevalence figures'. Japan: MHLW's guideline explicitly forbids fixing a number ('一律の剤数／種類数のみに着目するのではなく'), MHLW's fee notification quotes that same definition, and MHLW's payment rule then makes a bare count of six the sole trigger. England: NICE sets no threshold, the DES names condition-based cohorts, NHSBSA's measure spec is drug-only, and the paid indicators are drug-only. On the specific sub-question asked - whether count-based indicators displace condition-based ones near payment - the answer is yes, and in Japan it is documented by the regulator against its own stated position.

The contradiction is again US MTM: the condition axis was reinforced at the payment/regulatory layer in 2025, moving in the opposite direction to the predicted gradient. A weaker counter-signal points the same way: within the CMS Patient Safety suite the condition-bearing OMP measure is slated for retirement while the two drug-count polypharmacy measures were promoted into Star Ratings - but CMS gives a statistical reason (low rates, poor discrimination), not a binding-cost reason, so that case does not cleanly test the mechanism. I record Claim 3 as mixed rather than supported because one well-documented national instrument moves against it, and because England's terminal state (all SMR incentives abolished in 2023/24) removed both axes at once rather than the condition axis differentially.

One structural finding the hypothesis does not anticipate, which I flag because it recurs in every jurisdiction: this domain has a THIRD axis, laboratory and observation values (eGFR, K+, Na+, Ca2+, HbA1c, blood pressure, weight, creatinine clearance). It behaves like the drug axis, not like the condition axis - it survives into operational instruments (Scotland's STU indicators, England's paid SMR-03) - and for the same reason the hypothesis gives for drugs: results arrive pre-coded from pathology and observation feeds as a by-product of routine care. That is a confirmation of the mechanism, not of the two-axis taxonomy, and I would suggest the axis boundary is better drawn as 'criteria satisfiable from data generated pre-coded by an operational transaction' versus 'criteria requiring an interpretive clinical judgement to be recorded and coded for its own sake'.

domains.contradictions:
Three genuine contradictions found, plus two weaker counter-signals. I searched for them deliberately by looking for (a) instruments where a condition axis sits close to money, (b) decision-support systems that dropped the condition axis, and (c) cases where the condition axis was strengthened rather than weakened over time.

CONTRADICTION 1 (against Claims 2 and 3, strongest). US Medicare Part D MTM, 42 CFR 423.153(d)(2). A payment-layer regulatory requirement retained the condition axis AND strengthened it effective 1 January 2025, when CMS replaced sponsor discretion with a mandatory list of ten named chronic diseases (Alzheimer's, bone disease-arthritis, CHF, diabetes, dyslipidemia, ESRD, HIV/AIDS, hypertension, mental health, respiratory disease), while authoring no ICD-10 codes, no value set, and naming no code authority. This is condition-axis survival at the payment layer WITHOUT an authored binding, which Claim 2 says should not happen, and movement toward the condition axis near money, which Claim 3 says should not happen. My proposed reconciliation (delegated definition plus self-reported measurement, yielding enforceability without comparability) is a post hoc amendment to the hypothesis, and I flag it as such rather than presenting it as a rescue.

CONTRADICTION 2 (against the prior finding that decision support retains axis B). Korea's national DUR system. The MFDS designation regulation enumerates all nine national check categories - drug-drug, specific age band, pregnancy, dose, duration, therapeutic-class duplication, older-adult caution, lactation, tablet-splitting - and not one is diagnosis-dependent. This is a national clinical decision support instrument, i.e. far from payment, in which the condition axis does not exist at all. The prior PIM-domain tally recorded decision support retaining axis B 2 of 2; this domain supplies a national CDS at 0. It shows the layer gradient is not sufficient on its own: Scotland and Korea occupy the same layer and differ completely, and what differs between them is precisely whether a diagnosis binding was ever authored. So this case contradicts a simple layer-gradient reading while supporting the binding mechanism.

CONTRADICTION 3 (against the sharpness of the drug/condition dichotomy). The laboratory axis survives where the diagnosis axis does not, at every layer including payment. England's IIF SMR-03 - a paid indicator requiring 'a renal function test and a recording of their weight and Creatinine Clearance Rate' - and Scotland's STU indicators keyed on eGFR, K+, Na+, Ca2+, HbA1c and blood pressure both carry a patient-state criterion that is not a drug and not a diagnosis, and it survives. The two-axis taxonomy predicts nothing about this and would have to classify these as axis B, in which case axis B survives more often than Claim 1 states.

COUNTER-SIGNAL 4 (weak, against Claim 3). Within the CMS Patient Safety measure suite the condition-bearing measure (OMP, 'Use of Opioids from Multiple Providers in Persons Without Cancer', requiring an ICD-10 cancer exclusion) is flagged for retirement while the two pure drug-count polypharmacy measures were promoted from display measures into the Star Ratings programme for 2027. Directionally this supports Claim 3, but CMS's stated reason is statistical - 'very low measure rates, resulting in minimal opportunity for measure improvement' and 'the measure does not effectively discern good versus poor performance' - not the cost or absence of a binding. That is a competing explanation for the same observation and it weakens the causal reading of the gradient.

COUNTER-SIGNAL 5 (against reading England as differential loss). England's terminal state at the payment layer is not that the condition axis was dropped while the drug axis survived; it is that NHS England removed the SMR incentives from the IIF entirely for 2023/24, taking both axes with them. England therefore evidences which axis survived while payment existed, and does not evidence differential long-run survival. I could not retrieve the 2023/24 IIF guidance primary document, so I record this as inferred.

NEGATIVE FINDING WORTH STATING. I looked specifically for a national polypharmacy or medication-review instrument in which a body authored a diagnosis code list and applied it in the criterion, outside Scotland. In this domain I found exactly one clear instance, and it is not a polypharmacy indicator: England's RESP-01/RESP-02, which reuse the pre-existing QOF Asthma Register. I found no case in which a body authored a NEW diagnosis code list specifically for a polypharmacy or medication-review indicator. Scotland's binding is a general-purpose high-risk-prescribing binding that the polypharmacy indicators reuse; QOF's is a general-purpose disease register that the asthma indicators reuse. Every surviving condition axis I found was riding on a binding authored for some other purpose.
