domains.newHypotheses:
1. AMEND THE AXIS BOUNDARY: pre-coded-by-transaction versus recorded-for-its-own-sake. The drug/condition dichotomy misclassifies the laboratory axis, which survives operationalization as reliably as the drug axis does (England's paid SMR-03 requires renal function, weight and creatinine clearance; Scotland's STU indicators run on eGFR, K+, Na+, Ca2+, HbA1c and blood pressure). The property that actually predicts survival is not 'is it a drug' but 'is the datum generated pre-coded as a by-product of an operational transaction that has to happen anyway'. Dispensing generates drug codes; pathology generates result codes; billing generates procedure codes; enrollment generates hospice and ESRD status - CMS uses exactly that route for its polypharmacy measure exclusions. A diagnosis, by contrast, has to be entered by a clinician for no operational reason other than being recorded. This reframing explains the same asymmetry with one mechanism instead of two and correctly classifies the third axis the current taxonomy has no slot for.

2. TWO SURVIVAL ROUTES, NOT ONE, AND THEY PRODUCE DIFFERENT ARTEFACTS. Claim 2 assumes an authored binding is necessary. US MTM shows a second route: delegate both the operational definition and the measurement to the reporting entity, and collect the result by self-report. CMS took this route, and the Star Ratings measure that scores it (D11) has data source 'Part D Plan Reporting' and a denominator defined as 'the contracts' specified targeting criteria', whereas the drug-count measures in the same programme are computed centrally by CMS from PDE claims. The testable prediction is a clean dissociation: any nationally COMPUTED and cross-entity COMPARABLE indicator retaining a condition axis will have an authored national binding; any indicator retaining a condition axis WITHOUT one will turn out to be self-reported, or scored only for the fact of the activity rather than the fidelity of the targeting. This is falsifiable and would be tested by classifying every condition-axis-retaining instrument by data source rather than by layer.

3. THE THRESHOLD-INSERTION PHENOMENON, which may be the sharper finding in this domain than the loss of the condition axis. Every consensus source I read declined to set a numeric drug threshold, and two did so explicitly: NICE says only 'multiple medicines (polypharmacy)', and MHLW states '何剤からポリファーマシーとするかについて厳密な定義はなく' and warns against attending to '一律の剤数／種類数のみ'. Yet every operational layer inserted a number, and the numbers are mutually inconsistent across systems that cite the same evidence base: Japan 6, NHSBSA 8/10/15/20, England's DES and Scotland 10, US MTM up to 8. Operationalization is not only subtracting the condition axis, it is manufacturing a drug-count axis that the consensus source deliberately refused to provide. The mechanism is plausibly the same one - a threshold on a pre-coded count is computable and adjudicable, a clinical judgement is not - but the direction is additive rather than subtractive and the current hypothesis has no account of it. It also predicts that these thresholds should correlate with dispensing-data conventions in each system rather than with the clinical literature, which is checkable.

4. BINDINGS ARE INHERITED, NOT COMMISSIONED. In this entire domain I found no case where a body authored a new diagnosis code list specifically for a polypharmacy or medication-review indicator. Scotland's indicators reuse a general-purpose high-risk-prescribing binding held in EScro; England's RESP-01/02 reuse the QOF disease registers. This suggests the binary in Claim 2 ('did the operating body author a binding') should become a question about prior stock: a condition axis survives where the jurisdiction already holds a general-purpose, maintained, EHR-resident diagnosis binding that an indicator can be written against. That reframes the cross-national pattern as a function of primary-care coding infrastructure - which is why the UK nations and the US QOF-analogue programmes retain condition axes and Japan and Korea, whose national data spines are claims and dispensing rather than coded primary care records, do not. It predicts that the same clinical criterion will survive or die by jurisdiction independently of layer, which is directly testable against the Scotland-versus-Korea decision-support contrast I already found.

5. DELIBERATE EXCLUSION AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO INABILITY. Korea's DUR regulation enumerates nine check categories and none is diagnosis-based - and the enumeration is in a legal instrument, meaning the absence is a designed boundary, not an implementation shortfall. Before attributing all condition-axis loss to the cost of terminology work, it is worth testing a rival explanation: that operators exclude diagnosis-dependent rules because claims-recorded diagnoses in their system are known to be unreliable for clinical purposes (a well-documented concern in Korean claims data), and that they would decline the condition axis even if a binding were handed to them free. That rival is separable from the binding hypothesis and would be tested by finding a jurisdiction with a usable diagnosis binding that still declined to use it.

verdict.reasoning:
CLAIM 1 — SUPPORTED, with clean documented instances. The paediatric consensus source (KIDs List 2025) carries a condition/procedure axis in 8 of 39 drug rows (20.5%): viral illness for salicylates, post-tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy for codeine and tramadol, diaper dermatitis for potent topical corticosteroids, acute infectious diarrhoea for loperamide, pertussis/Chlamydia/Ureaplasma exceptions for macrolides, gonococcal exception for ceftriaxone, postpartum resuscitation for naloxone. Korea's national paediatric contraindication instrument (특정연령대금기, 210 ingredients) retains ZERO of those condition axes while retaining the age axis in full, and grew from 105 to 210 ingredients between 2010 and 2026 on the drug/age axis alone. Wales converts the salicylate rule into 'Number of patients under 16 with a current prescription of aspirin' — the drug and the age threshold survive, the viral-illness condition is deleted. On the pregnancy side the asymmetry is even sharper: Korea's 임부금기 list carries a fully enumerated 1,236-ingredient drug axis and a condition axis present in only 22 rows (1.8%), all free text, with ZERO trimester qualifiers; England's and Wales's national valproate/retinoid/topiramate indicators carry a complete BNF code list for the drug and reduce the condition to sex plus an age band.

CLAIM 2 — MIXED, and the mechanism needs generalising. The binding half is strongly confirmed. Every instrument in my domain that RETAINED a condition axis had a body that authored and applied an operational definition: HIRA writes KCD ranges into the indicator titles (J00-J06, J09-J18, J30-J47) and authors exclusion sets (K20-K93, C15-C26, M00-M25, M40-M54); NCQA/CMS bind pharyngitis, comorbid conditions and competing diagnoses to VSAC value sets in CMS146v12; Wales binds the one condition it kept in the female indicator block to code sets in so many words, 'without any hysterectomy READ/SNOMED codes'. Every instrument that LOST it lacked one, and NHSBSA states the reason outright: 'Clearly some females in this age band are permanently unable to get pregnant (e.g. have had a hysterectomy) but such patients cannot be identified from the prescribing data used to populate this dashboard.' Korea is the instructive intermediate: HIRA transmits both a diagnosis code (질병분류기호, 주 상병코드) and a pregnancy flag (임부여부) in the DUR message and even returns the relevant diagnosis as display text, yet applies no rule, expressly handing the judgment to the prescriber — '상병에 따라 처방의사가 1등급 또는 2등급으로 판단하여 사유기재 여부 결정'. Authored-but-not-applied degrades to not-retained, exactly as the claim predicts. I score MIXED for two reasons. First, the binding need not be a TERMINOLOGY binding: iPLEDGE retains the pregnancy axis at the dispensing gate through a laboratory-test-plus-registry operational definition (two negative pregnancy tests, 7-day prescription window) and no diagnosis codes at all. Second, 42 CFR 456.705(b)(2) mandates drug-disease contraindication screening as a federal condition of payment while CMS authors nothing, explicitly delegating the standards to 'the State or its contractor' and 'commercial vendors of DUR services'. The operating body need not be the authoring body.

CLAIM 3 — CONTRADICTED in this domain, and the gradient partly runs the other way. Axis B survives AT the payment layer in four independent jurisdictions: Japan's 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 is a line item in the national fee schedule that simultaneously requires an indication set (急性気道感染症、急性中耳炎、急性副鼻腔炎又は急性下痢症), a comorbidity condition (基礎疾患のない患者), an exclusion diagnosis set (influenza, COVID-19) and an age limit; CMS146v12 carries comorbid-condition and competing-diagnosis exclusions into MIPS; 42 CFR 456.705 makes drug-disease screening a condition of federal financial participation; iPLEDGE makes pregnancy status the literal precondition of dispensing. Meanwhile axis B is lost at layers FAR from money: England's NHSBSA paediatric antimicrobial stewardship dashboard (a pure reporting product with no payment consequence) has no condition axis at all — zero occurrences of 'diagnosis', 'indication', 'Read code' or 'SNOMED' in the whole specification; Wales's non-payment National Prescribing Indicators strip the viral-illness condition off the aspirin rule; Scotland's polypharmacy guideline reduces valproate-in-pregnancy to a narrative prompt. The variable that separates the survivors from the casualties is not distance to money, it is DATA PROVENANCE. Instruments built on CLAIMS data (Korea HIRA, Japan MHLW, US CMS/NCQA) keep the condition axis, because a diagnosis has to be recorded to justify payment in the first place. Instruments built on DISPENSING or PRESCRIBING data (NHSBSA, AWTTC) lose it, because those datasets never carried a diagnosis. Since payment is precisely what causes diagnoses to be coded, proximity to money predicts axis-B survival POSITIVELY here, not negatively.

domains.contradictions:
Four substantive contradictions, plus two refinements that weaken the hypothesis as stated.

1. AXIS B SURVIVING AT THE PAYMENT LAYER — Japan. 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 is a fee-schedule add-on (80 points) in the FY2024 MHLW notice 保医発0305第4号 別添1, and its eligibility test is almost entirely condition-based: '急性気道感染症、急性中耳炎、急性副鼻腔炎又は急性下痢症により受診した基礎疾患のない患者であって、診察の結果、抗菌薬の投与の必要性が認められないため抗菌薬を使用しないもの' with an explicit exclusion diagnosis set '...インフルエンザウイルス感染の患者又はインフルエンザウイルス感染の疑われる患者及び新型コロナウイルス感染症の患者又は新型コロナウイルス感染症が疑われる患者については、算定できない.' Four condition constructs (indication set, comorbidity state, exclusion diagnoses, age) all survive into the layer closest to money. Claim 3 predicts the opposite.

2. AXIS B SURVIVING AT THE PAYMENT LAYER — United States, twice. (a) 42 CFR 456.705(b)(2) makes 'Drug-disease contraindication' a mandatory point-of-sale screen and a condition of federal financial participation for Medicaid — the condition axis is not merely retained near money, it is compelled by money. (b) CMS146v12 carries NCQA-authored 'comorbid condition' and 'competing diagnosis' value-set exclusions into MIPS payment adjustment, with an explicit 3-17 year paediatric stratum.

3. AXIS B LOST AT THE LAYER FURTHEST FROM MONEY — England and Wales. The NHSBSA Antimicrobial Stewardship Children dashboard has no payment consequence whatever and has a completely empty condition axis (ASC01-ASC05 are all drug x age; zero mentions of diagnosis, indication, Read code or SNOMED in the entire specification). Wales's National Prescribing Indicators carry no payment consequence and still delete the viral-illness condition from the aspirin/Reye rule. Scotland's polypharmacy guidance sits at the guideline layer and contains no pregnancy or paediatric indicator at all. The gradient in this domain does not run from guideline to payment; it runs from claims-based data to dispensing-based data.

4. THE BINDING NEED NOT BE A TERMINOLOGY BINDING. iPLEDGE retains the pregnancy condition axis absolutely, at the dispensing gate, with FDA as author — and uses no ICD, SNOMED or value set. The operational definition is a laboratory test plus a time window plus a registry authorization. Claim 2 as written ('a value set / code list / operational definition mapping the clinical condition to diagnosis codes') would score this as no-binding and predict loss; the axis is in fact the strongest-surviving condition axis I found anywhere in the domain.

5. THE OPERATING BODY NEED NOT BE THE AUTHORING BODY. CMS mandates drug-disease screening under 42 CFR 456.705 while explicitly declining to author the standards (§456.703(e): 'Developed directly by the State or its contractor; Obtained by the State through contracts with commercial vendors of DUR services'). Claim 2's 'some body AUTHORED ... AND APPLIED it in the indicator definition' survives only if 'some body' is read very loosely.

6. A CONTRADICTION OF MY OWN DOMAIN FRAMING, reported for honesty. Most of the surviving condition axes above are INDICATION conditions (pharyngitis, otitis media, URI, acute diarrhoea), not CONTRAINDICATION comorbidities. The one clear surviving CONTRAINDICATION comorbidity in a national paediatric/pregnancy instrument is Wales's 'female patients with a past medical history of venous or arterial thrombosis who have been prescribed combined hormonal contraceptives' — and that is a contraceptive-safety rule, not a teratogenicity rule. If the analysis is restricted to contraindication-type conditions, Claim 3 looks much less contradicted. I flag this because it materially changes the verdict and a reader should be able to re-score it.

WHAT I SEARCHED FOR AND DID NOT FIND: I looked specifically for a national indicator anywhere that binds PREGNANCY (or pregnancy intention, or contraception status) to a diagnosis/observation code and applies it to a teratogenic medicine. I found none in England (NHSBSA valproate spec: sex+age), Wales (valproate/retinoids/topiramate: sex+age), Scotland (narrative only), Korea (a prescriber-entered 임부여부 flag), Japan (妊婦加算 abolished; nothing replaced it) or the US federal Medicaid minimum standards (no drug-pregnancy category at all). That negative result is consistent across every jurisdiction I could reach.

domains.newHypotheses:
DATA-PROVENANCE HYPOTHESIS (proposed replacement for Claim 3, and a generalisation of Claim 2).

A condition-dependent criterion survives operationalisation if and only if the condition is already recorded, in coded form, in the dataset the instrument is built on — for a reason independent of the safety rule. Drugs arrive pre-coded because dispensing and reimbursement require it. Diagnoses arrive pre-coded ONLY where a claim has to be justified. Therefore:

- Claims-based instruments retain axis B. Korea HIRA (KCD on every 청구 line), Japan MHLW (傷病名 on every レセプト), US CMS/NCQA (ICD-10-CM and value sets on every encounter) all retain it, and all three sit at or adjacent to payment.
- Dispensing-based instruments lose axis B and substitute whatever demographic attribute travels with the prescription. NHSBSA and AWTTC both substitute sex + age band, and NHSBSA says so in writing.
- Prescriber-attested attributes are an unstable middle ground. Korea's DUR carries 임부여부 as a transmitted flag and carries 주상병코드 in the same message, yet applies neither to the 임부금기 grading, which it hands back to the prescriber. The axis exists in the data pipe and still dies in the rule.

Under this hypothesis, distance to money predicts axis-B survival POSITIVELY, because payment is the very mechanism that causes conditions to be coded. The prior PIM finding (axis B lost at payment layers) and my finding (axis B kept at payment layers) are then not in conflict: PIM contraindication comorbidities are conditions nobody is paid to code at the moment of prescribing, whereas antibiotic-stewardship indications are conditions that constitute the claim itself.

COROLLARY — PREGNANCY IS THE PATHOLOGICAL CASE. Pregnancy is neither a dispensing attribute nor, for a non-obstetric encounter, a reliably recorded billing diagnosis. So every jurisdiction I reached falls back to one of exactly three substitutes: (i) a demographic proxy (England, Wales: female, 13-54 or ≤55), (ii) a prescriber-asserted flag (Korea: 임부여부), or (iii) a purpose-built registry keyed on a laboratory test (US: iPLEDGE, two negative pregnancy tests and a 7-day window). Substitute (iii) is the only one that actually enforces the rule, and it is also by far the most expensive — which predicts that it will only ever be built for a handful of drugs with catastrophic and unambiguous teratogenicity (isotretinoin, thalidomide-class agents), never for the 1,236-ingredient Korean 임부금기 list or the 4-in-10 risk of valproate.

TESTABLE PREDICTION. If the data-provenance hypothesis is right, then a jurisdiction that begins capturing pregnancy status as a coded observation in primary-care records should, within a few revision cycles, produce a national indicator that uses it. The English SNOMED CT primary-care record does carry pregnancy concepts; the NHSBSA dashboard does not use them because it is built on the dispensing warehouse rather than the GP record. A GP-record-based instrument in England (a PINCER-style indicator rather than an ePACT2 comparator) should therefore be able to retain the axis. PINCER already demonstrates the capability with Read/SNOMED code bindings for peptic ulcer, asthma and heart failure — it simply has no paediatric or pregnancy indicator in its national set. That is a falsifiable, cheap test of the mechanism.

SECOND HYPOTHESIS — AGE IS NOT AXIS B, IT IS AXIS A. Much of what reads as condition-dependence in paediatric criteria is actually age- or weight-dependence, and age and weight behave like drugs, not like diseases: they are administrative attributes attached to the patient record for independent reasons. This is why Korea could operationalise 210 age-contraindicated ingredients with no difficulty at all while operationalising zero paediatric disease-contraindicated ones. Any future coding of these criteria sets should score age/weight/gestational-age thresholds as axis A, or the asymmetry will be systematically understated.

domains.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults (condition-dependent glycaemic targets; sulfonylurea/insulin in dementia, frailty and hypoglycaemia-risk patients)

verdict.reasoning:
CLAIM 1 (asymmetry) — MIXED, and the verdict flips depending on how axis B is read.

Under the STRICT reading (axis B = 'avoid drug X in patients WITH condition Y'), Claim 1 holds cleanly. I found exactly ONE national instrument anywhere that implements a drug×condition hypoglycaemia rule operationally: Scotland's STU/RDS case-finding indicators ('Patient with diabetes type 2 and dementia' × 'sulfonylurea, gliptin, meglitinide, GLP1RA, insulin' × 'HbA1c <53'). It sits at the decision-support layer. Zero measure-specification, public-rating or payment instruments in England, the US, Korea, Japan or Germany carry a drug×condition hypoglycaemia rule. Drug-only rules, by contrast, survive readily: Scotland's NTI 'sulfonylureas in people aged ≥75', HIRA's 인슐린 처방률, and CMS816 (denominator = 'at least one hypoglycemic medication administration', exclusions 'None') all sit at rating or payment layers.

Under the BROADER reading actually specified for this domain (condition-dependent HbA1c targets count as axis B), Claim 1 is contradicted at the layer where it should bite hardest. England's QOF — the closest-to-money instrument I examined — retains the condition axis in full (DM020/DM021, frailty-split targets, 17 and 10 points) while the DRUG axis is entirely absent: a grep of the whole QOF 2025/26 guidance for 'hypoglyc', 'sulfonylurea', 'sulphonylurea' and 'insulin' returns zero hits. So in England's payment instrument the asymmetry runs the OPPOSITE way from Claim 1: condition retained, drug dropped. The same inversion holds for CMS122v13 (frailty + advanced illness exclusion retained; no drug axis).

CLAIM 2 (mechanism) — SUPPORTED, with one qualified exception. Every case where the condition axis survived into a computable definition is accompanied by an authored, applied terminology binding: Scotland maps 'each element of the criteria within the indicator to clinical codes used in the primary care patient record – read codes (which in turn map to SNOMED-CT codes) and the Dictionary of Medicines and Devices (DM&D)'; NHS Digital publishes MODFRAIL_COD (2 SNOMED concepts) and SEVFRAIL_COD (3 concepts) as Primary Care Domain refsets, and QOF business rules 'are based entirely on SNOMED codes'; NCQA authored and applied Frailty Diagnosis / Frailty Symptom / Frailty Device / Frailty Encounter / Advanced Illness / Dementia Medications value sets under its own OID root in CMS122v13. Conversely, every case where the condition axis was LOST is an instrument computed over a substrate lacking condition codes: Scotland's NTIs ('use prescription data'), and Korea's HbA1c control rate (claims + a single HbA1c value in 특정내역 MT057, with frailty collapsed to '65세 이상'). The consensus sources confirm the premise from the other side: ADA 2026 concedes verbatim 'there is no global consensus on the optimal classification strategy' for its own Table 13.2 categories, and specifies no codes at all.

The mechanism also shows a recurring workaround that Claim 2 predicts: where a condition is not reliably coded, operators substitute a DRUG PROXY, because drugs arrive pre-coded. Scotland defines dementia as 'Documented dementia (or on donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine or memantine)'; NCQA's CMS122 accepts 'taking dementia medications' as advanced-illness evidence; PQA's SUPD identifies diabetes itself by two medication fills.

The qualified exception is Germany. The DMP-A-RL retains the condition axis and its quality indicator ('Anteil ... deren individuell vereinbarter HbA1c-Wert erreicht wird') without authoring any binding at all — the condition is never coded and the individualised target is never recorded; only a clinician-declared 'Zielwert erreicht / Zielwert noch nicht erreicht' flag reaches the data. Axis B survives in name but is unauditable and cannot distinguish appropriate individualisation from overtreatment. I count this as a partial contradiction: survival without a binding is possible, but only in a hollow form.

CLAIM 3 (gradient toward payment) — CONTRADICTED in this domain. The two strongest, best-bound retentions of the condition axis are the two instruments closest to money: QOF DM020/DM021 (direct GP payment, 27 points combined, frailty defined by NHSD SNOMED refsets) and CMS122v13 in the Medicare Quality Payment Program (frailty + advanced illness exclusion via NCQA value sets). Meanwhile the condition axis was LOST in an instrument with NO payment attached — Scotland's National Therapeutic Indicators, a published benchmarking series, where 'Sulfonylurea use in frail older adults' is computed as 'aged ≥ 75 years prescribed sulfonylureas'. Layer tallies from what I verified: guideline 3/3 retained; decision-support 2/2 retained; measure-specification 3/3 retained (one of them, Germany, hollow); public-rating 1/4 retained (GSD, and that only 'inferred'); payment 2/3 retained. The gradient, if anything, runs the wrong way — retention is LOWEST at public rating, not at payment.

domains.contradictions:
Actively hunted and found five distinct contradictions.

(1) AGAINST CLAIM 3, the strongest case: England's QOF is the payment instrument par excellence and it retains the condition axis with a full SNOMED binding. Verbatim, from the NHS England QOF 2025/26 guidance: "DM021. The percentage of patients with diabetes, on the register, with moderate or severe frailty in whom the last IFCC-HbA1c is 75 mmol/mol or less in the preceding 12 months" — 10 points, thresholds 52–92%. Frailty is bound by NHSD refsets I downloaded in full (MODFRAIL_COD = SNOMED 1129381000000102 'Canadian Study of Health and Aging Clinical Frailty Scale level 6 - moderately frail' and 925831000000107 'Moderate frailty'; SEVFRAIL_COD = CFS levels 7 and 8 plus 'Severe frailty'). If money killed axis B, this indicator would not exist.

(2) AGAINST CLAIM 3, second case: CMS122v13 / MIPS Quality ID #001 sits in the Medicare Quality Payment Program and retains the condition axis via NCQA value sets: "Exclude patients 66 and older by the end of the measurement period with an indication of frailty for any part of the measurement period who also meet any of the following advanced illness criteria."

(3) AGAINST CLAIM 3, reverse direction: axis B was lost at a layer FAR from money. Scotland's National Therapeutic Indicators carry no payment consequence and are pure benchmarking, yet the indicator titled "Increase Falls Risk: Sulfonylurea use in frail older adults" is computed as "Number of people aged ≥ 75 years prescribed sulfonylureas as a percentage of all people aged ≥ 75 years prescribed an anti-diabetic drug". The frailty condition is dropped at a non-payment layer, in the same jurisdiction and by the same programme that retains it in decision support.

(4) AGAINST CLAIM 1's asymmetry direction: in England's payment instrument the DRUG axis is the one that vanished, not the condition axis. The complete QOF 2025/26 guidance contains zero occurrences of 'hypoglyc', 'sulfonylurea', 'sulphonylurea' or 'insulin'. Same inversion in CMS122v13 (condition exclusion present, no drug axis) and in the German DMP quality-indicator set (condition-dependent target present, no drug×condition indicator).

(5) AGAINST CLAIM 2 as literally stated: Germany's G-BA DMP-A-RL retains axis B — "Bei Patientenwunsch, bei fortgeschrittenem Alter, bei Multimorbidität, Hypoglykämiegefährdung ... kann ein HbA1c-Ziel bis 8,5 % (69 mmol/mol) ... tolerabel sein" — and carries it into a quality indicator, "Anteil von Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern, deren individuell vereinbarter HbA1c-Wert erreicht wird", with NO terminology binding whatsoever. The only trace in the data is documentation field 20, "HbA1c-Zielwert | Zielwert erreicht / Zielwert noch nicht erreicht". So a body CAN retain axis B without authoring a binding — by delegating the classification to the clinician. I judge this a hollow retention (the indicator cannot distinguish an appropriately relaxed target from overtreatment), but it is a real counterexample to the stated mechanism.

Also searched for and did NOT find any contradiction of the following kind: no national measure-specification, public rating or payment instrument in any of the six jurisdictions implements a drug×condition hypoglycaemia rule (e.g. 'avoid sulfonylureas/insulin in patients with dementia'). The one operational implementation anywhere is Scotland's decision-support layer. I also found no national instrument in any jurisdiction that measures glycaemic OVERTREATMENT (an HbA1c lower bound in patients on hypoglycaemia-causing drugs) — despite ADA 13.14a, MHLW and G-BA all recommending exactly that. Korea's indicator has no lower bound; England's QOF has none; the NDA has none; HEDIS GSD/EDH have none.
domains.unassessable:
Tooling constraints: my WebSearch budget (200 calls) was consumed early by the orchestration harness before I had covered all jurisdictions, and the fallback engines then rate-limited (DuckDuckGo lite/html served bot challenges, Mojeek and Ecosia 403, Startpage and searx served JS challenges, Bing returned no parseable results, Brave worked for roughly a dozen queries then began returning a single unrelated result). Several target sites also block automated retrieval: nice.org.uk and hira.or.kr yielded to curl with a browser user-agent; england.nhs.uk PDFs required the r.jina.ai reader proxy; digital.nhs.uk, ncqa.org and diabetesjournals.org returned 403 to curl and WebFetch alike (I recovered NCQA EDH and the ADA text via the reader proxy and PMC respectively).

Specifically could not obtain:
1. The JDS/JGS joint categorised glycaemic-target table itself (高齢者の血糖コントロール目標, 2016) — the single most important drug×condition consensus artefact in this domain, since it sets HbA1c LOWER limits conditional on use of insulin/sulfonylureas/glinides and on cognitive/ADL category. jds.or.jp candidate URLs 404'd. I have only MHLW's verbatim reference to its existence. Its own coding status is therefore unassessable and conditionCount is left null.
2. Recent National Diabetes Audit editions (2022-23 onward). digital.nhs.uk is fully blocked by all three retrieval routes. I verified the 2016-17 edition only, so I cannot say whether the NDA has since adopted the QOF frailty split. Treat my NDA row as evidence about 2016-17, not about today.
3. NCQA's own HEDIS technical specification for GSD (paywalled/WAF-blocked) — marked 'inferred'.
4. PQA's SUPD measure specification (member-gated) — marked 'inferred', included only as a mechanism illustration.
5. Australia entirely. I could not reach the PIP QI Improvement Measures technical specifications on health.gov.au (connection failed) and had no search budget left to locate a mirror. No Australian row is reported rather than guessing.
6. Israel's QICH diabetes indicator specifications. The public domain page lists only "primary prevention: cholesterol, blood pressure, and glucose balance" and "secondary prevention" categories with no HbA1c threshold, age stratum, or hypoglycaemia/overtreatment indicator visible; I could not obtain the underlying specification, so I report no row.
7. Canada, the Netherlands, the Nordic diabetes registries, NHS Wales QAIF and Northern Ireland — not reached at all.
8. England's PINCER/SMASH prescribing-safety indicator set for this domain. The PRIMIS page 404'd and I could not confirm from a primary source whether PINCER contains any diabetes/hypoglycaemia indicator. I make no claim either way.
9. The Endocrine Society 2019 'Treatment of Diabetes in Older Adults' guideline as a second consensus source — not retrieved.
10. The Korean Diabetes Association clinical practice guideline as a primary consensus source — I have only HIRA's verbatim citation of it ("노인 당뇨에서 혈당조절 목표는 당화혈색소 7.5% 미만임 (2021 당뇨병 진료지침, 대한당뇨병학회)"), not the guideline text.
11. Whether Scotland's 69 case-finding indicator specifications include a published, downloadable code list per indicator. The guidance says the specifications exist and live in the EScro database; I read the indicator-level denominator/numerator definitions in the published 'Polypharmacy Indicators' PDF but not the underlying Read/SNOMED code sets themselves.
domains.newHypotheses:
SUBSTRATE DETERMINISM beats the money gradient. In this domain, which axis survives operationalisation is predicted almost perfectly by the DATA SUBSTRATE the instrument is computed over, and not at all by distance from payment.

- Instruments computed over dispensing/pharmacy-claims data (Scotland's National Therapeutic Indicators; Korea's HIRA claims-based assessment; PQA's Part D measures; CMS816's medication-administration denominator) retain the DRUG axis and lose or age-proxy the CONDITION axis — regardless of whether money is attached (NTIs: no money, axis B lost; HIRA: money, axis B lost; CMS816: money, axis B never present).
- Instruments computed over structured EHR/GP-record data (Scotland's STU/RDS; England's QOF; US eCQMs) retain the CONDITION axis — again regardless of money (STU: no money, axis B retained; QOF: maximum money, axis B retained).

This reframes Claim 2 correctly and makes Claim 3 an artefact. The binding is not the cause; it is the observable trace of a substrate that can carry conditions at all. A body authors a frailty refset when its extraction runs against SNOMED-coded GP records, and does not bother when its extraction runs against dispensing lines. Prediction: in jurisdictions where national quality measurement is claims-based (Korea, Japan, US Part D), axis B will be lost or age-proxied at EVERY layer including guideline-adjacent ones; in jurisdictions with a national primary-care EHR extract (UK nations), axis B will survive at every layer including payment. My six jurisdictions fit this without exception.

TWO SECONDARY MECHANISMS worth adding to the framework:

(a) DRUG-PROXY RESCUE. When a condition is poorly coded, operators do not drop it — they re-express it as a drug. Scotland: 'Documented dementia (or on donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine or memantine)'. NCQA in CMS122v13: advanced illness can be met by 'taking dementia medications', via the 'Dementia Medications' value set. PQA SUPD: diabetes itself is identified by two diabetes medication fills. This is Claim 2's premise ('drugs arrive pre-coded') operating as a repair strategy rather than as a failure mode, and it means measured 'axis B retention' will systematically over-represent conditions that have a signature drug (dementia, Parkinson's) and under-represent those that do not (frailty, functional impairment, food insecurity).

(b) AXIS-B DEGRADATION LADDER — retention is not binary. Ranked from strongest to weakest, this domain shows four grades: (i) coded drug×condition rule with authored code list (Scotland STU/RDS); (ii) coded condition-stratified target with authored refset (QOF DM020/DM021; CMS122 exclusion); (iii) age-proxied condition (Scotland NTI 'frail' → ≥75; HIRA 'elderly' → ≥65; ADA/KDA comorbidity strata → a single age cut); (iv) clinician-declared condition with no binding at all (Germany's 'individuell vereinbarter HbA1c-Wert erreicht'). Grades (iii) and (iv) both look like 'retained' in a coarse coding scheme but are epistemically empty — grade (iii) cannot identify the frail, and grade (iv) cannot be audited. I recommend the parent study score axis-B retention on this four-grade ladder rather than as a boolean; otherwise Germany and Korea will be miscoded and the layer gradient will be noise.

A DOMAIN-SPECIFIC ASYMMETRY worth flagging separately: the DIRECTION of the rule matters more than the axis. Every national instrument I verified measures UNDERtreatment (HbA1c too high) or a downstream HARM (severe hypoglycaemia events, ED visits). Not one measures OVERtreatment — no national instrument in England, the US, Korea, Japan, Germany or Scotland places a lower bound on HbA1c in patients taking insulin or sulfonylureas, despite ADA 13.14a, the MHLW guidance and the G-BA directive all recommending exactly that. The frailty-stratified QOF/NICE pair looks like an overtreatment safeguard but is not one: DM021's numerator rewards HbA1c ≤75 mmol/mol in frail patients, so a frail patient at 45 mmol/mol on gliclazide scores as a success. The condition axis survived; the safety rule it was carrying did not.
